thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging emma-oncall (on-call). Detected spike in NXDOMAINs for api.redwood.ai from EU region via our GeoDNS probe group. Error rate 18% over baseline. Auto-escalation rules triggered.

emma-oncall: ack. I’m online. Adding notes to incident channel.

ryan-netops: seeing the same from our resolvers — NXDOMAINs mostly hitting eu-west-1 and eu-central probes. client-side failures (RCODE=3) rather than timeouts.

priya-sre: can we confirm whether this is backend or DNS provider? start with dig from our probe cluster and from Cloudflare and Route53 health checks.

lucas-mlinfra: ran quick dig from our eu probe:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.ai A +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
```
Also did an authoritative query to our zone NS in route53 and got NXDOMAIN for some RRsets.

maya-cs: multiple customers in EU reporting 5xx and "domain not found" errors in logs. Is this causing client retries and higher latency?

emma-oncall: customer impact = partial (10-20% of EU traffic). Surface on status page as "partial outage - DNS resolution"? thoughts @alex-product

alex-product: yes mark partial and call out EU region. Put ETA unknown and we’ll update when we have cause.

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare reports no widespread outage in Europe. Some isolated resolver degradations in DE region (infra team investigating).

route53-monitor: Route53 console shows elevated SERVFAIL/NoData metrics for the hosted zone for ~20m, coincident with our probe spike. No known service incident listed.

ryan-netops: hypothesis: inconsistent zone answers between our GeoDNS control plane and one of the authoritative providers (Route53) due to a partial propagation or a bad change that created an empty RRset. Could be TTL flip / bad deploy.

priya-sre: check recent deploys/zone updates. @lucas-mlinfra did anyone push zone changes in last 30m?

lucas-mlinfra: nothing from infra team. The last zone edit was 2h ago (weight update) — I’ll pull change history now.

emma-oncall: while we debug, suggest short-term mitigation: route traffic away from affected resolvers via GeoDNS weights, set eu weight to 0 for api record so clients fall back to other regions. This reduces immediate client errors at cost of latency for EU users. ok to proceed?

priya-sre: agree. Also reduce TTL to 30s on the record in case we need to flip things quickly.

ryan-netops: I can change weights via rdw-geodns tool: `rdw-geodns set-weight api.redwood.ai eu 0` then validate. I’ll run now.

ryan-netops: (runs) `rdw-geodns set-weight api.redwood.ai eu 0` -> success.

route53-monitor: Route53 record still returning NXDOMAIN from some nameservers; our rdw-geodns change is in the control plane but external caches may still hit bad answers for up to TTL.

priya-sre: lowering TTL to 30s on authoritative record now so caches expire faster. Command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://ttl-30.json`

lucas-mlinfra: change submitted to Route53, change id: CAZQEXAMPLE. ETA propagation ~ 60s -> watchers please re-run dig probes.

emma-oncall: rerun probes now and post counts.

ryan-netops: pre-change NXDOMAIN rate from eu probes 18%. post-change initial probe run shows 6%. continuing to improve.

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare probe showing decreased NXDOMAINs from 15% -> 4% after TTL change.

maya-cs: customer messages are calming down, only a few lingering error traces. I’m updating support thread to say we’re mitigating and to expect intermittent failures for ~10-15m.

priya-sre: good. Can we identify the root cause? Why did authoritative NS return NXDOMAIN for valid record? Need to check zone integrity on all NS and Rule evaluation in our GeoDNS control plane.

lucas-mlinfra: pulling zone file across all authoritative nameservers now, comparing serials and RRset presence.

lucas-mlinfra: quick diff: one Route53 nameserver cluster (ns-3) returned an empty RRset for the weighted A record — looks like a partial replication lag inside Route53 or a transient internal inconsistency. The change history doesn’t show a delete.

ryan-netops: contacted AWS support with trace and dig outputs. They acknowledged and say they’re investigating replication within the hosted zone cluster.

priya-sre: Slack-note to AWS support: included change id, dig outputs, timestamps, and last known good serial. Requesting expedited replication fix or rollback of the inconsistent cluster.

emma-oncall: thanks. For now keep eu weight 0 until AWS confirms fix. We should also add a temporary resolver-level heuristic: if >10% NXDOMAIN from a resolver pool, consider marking it unhealthy for GeoDNS. I’ll file a post-incident action.

alex-product: status page update please: partial outage - DNS resolution impact in EU - mitigated by traffic reroute, TTL lowered, AWS investigating.

maya-cs: done — posted update, included recommended customer workaround (retry, fallback) and link to support ticket.

cloudflare-status-bot: Cloudflare resolution metrics show NXDOMAIN rate back to baseline after ~12m.

route53-monitor: AWS support updated: internal replication lag resolved, inconsistent NS cluster fixed at ~4176543260. They did not have an immediate RCA yet.

priya-sre: re-run dig against all NS; verify RRset presence and then restore GeoDNS weights slowly.

ryan-netops: verified all NS return correct RRset now. I’ll start undimming EU weight: `rdw-geodns set-weight api.redwood.ai eu 1` (gradual)

ryan-netops: ramp done. Probes show healthy resolution rates.

emma-oncall: switching incident state to "mitigated" and keeping monitoring for 1h before close. Will assign postmortem to me and ryan.

alex-product: assign follow-ups: (1) add resolver health heuristic to geodns control plane (2) improve monitoring to detect NXDOMAIN bursts earlier (3) run a tabletop on external DNS provider failures.

maya-cs: tagging customers touched, sending follow-up proactively.

priya-sre: adding mitigation steps to playbook: include TTL-drop + weight-0 fallback + contact template for AWS.

emma-oncall: thanks team. Handing off to ryan for watch. If anything pops during the watch window ping me @emma-oncall.

ryan-netops: ack, I’ll watch for 1h then hand to next oncall if stable.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 4176543265. Incident channel will remain open for follow-ups.

maya-cs: great work everyone :thumbsup:
